experiments.title: Single Layer Perceptron for Binary Classification
experiments.aim: Design and implement a single layer perceptron from scratch and using Keras/PyTorch to classify linearly separable data (AND/OR logic gates).
experiments.description: Implement decision boundary learning for linearly separable logic gates using step activation functions and perceptron learning rule.
expectedOutputs: Linear decision boundary plot separating logic truth tables
experiments.starterPrompt: Implement AND and OR perceptrons from scratch and with PyTorch or Keras. Set random seeds, train until all four truth-table rows are correct, print predictions and targets for each implementation, assert exact equality, and plot decision boundaries. Tiny truth tables may use up to 2000 training updates, with bounded convergence.

experiments.title: Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) for XOR Classification
experiments.aim: Implement a Multilayer Perceptron with backpropagation to solve the non-linearly separable XOR problem using PyTorch or Keras.
experiments.description: Demonstrate how hidden layers and non-linear activations (Sigmoid/ReLU) overcome the single-layer perceptron limitation on XOR data.
expectedOutputs: Final model predictions matching XOR truth table
experiments.starterPrompt: Implement a Multilayer Perceptron using PyTorch or Keras to solve the XOR logic classification problem. Train the network, show epoch loss progression, and display the predicted probability outputs for all 4 inputs.

experiments.title: Mini-Batch Gradient Descent & Optimization Algorithms
experiments.aim: Compare Batch, Mini-Batch, and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) with Adam and RMSProp optimizers on a synthetic regression/classification dataset.
experiments.description: Study how batch size and adaptive momentum optimizers affect training convergence speed, oscillation, and final generalization loss.
expectedOutputs: Comparative training loss curves (SGD vs Mini-Batch vs Adam)
experiments.starterPrompt: Compare Batch GD (full batch), stochastic GD (batch size 1), mini-batch GD (batch size 32), Adam, and RMSProp on the same seeded synthetic data. Plot all five loss curves and parameter trajectories, and print the convergence benchmark table. Use every optimizer named in the aim.

experiments.title: Deep Feedforward Neural Network for Multi-Class Classification
experiments.aim: Build and train a Deep Feedforward Neural Network with multiple hidden layers, Dropout, and Batch Normalization for multi-class classification.
experiments.description: Design a multi-layer deep network using Softmax activation, Categorical Crossentropy loss, and Xavier/He weight initialization.
experiments.starterPrompt: Construct a deep neural network for multi-class classification with 3 hidden layers, Batch Normalization, and Dropout. Plot loss curves and output the test accuracy and classification report.

experiments.title: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for Image Classification
experiments.aim: Design a Convolutional Neural Network with Conv2D, MaxPooling, and Dense layers for image classification on the MNIST/Fashion-MNIST dataset.
experiments.description: Construct feature extraction pipelines with spatial convolutions and pooling filters to classify 2D handwritten digits or clothing items.
expectedOutputs: Conv2D feature map dimensions & parameter summary
Sample predictions grid with ground-truth vs predicted labels
experiments.starterPrompt: Build and evaluate a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for MNIST handwritten digit recognition. Include Convolution, MaxPool, Flatten, and Dense layers. Train for 5 epochs and display sample predictions with accuracy.

experiments.title: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN & LSTM) for Sequence Modeling
experiments.aim: Implement SimpleRNN and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for time-series forecasting or text sequence prediction.
experiments.description: Address the vanishing gradient problem with gating mechanisms (LSTM/GRU) to model long-range temporal dependencies in sequence data.
expectedOutputs: Time-series prediction vs ground-truth comparison chart
experiments.starterPrompt: Train and compare SimpleRNN and LSTM on the same seeded time series split. Plot predictions and loss, report RMSE and MAE, and show hidden state shapes.

experiments.title: Transfer Learning with Pretrained Vision Models
experiments.aim: Fine-tune a pretrained deep network (MobileNetV2 or ResNet50) using feature extraction and fine-tuning for custom classification tasks.
experiments.description: Freeze base convolutional weights, add custom classification heads, and unfreeze top layers for fine-tuning with low learning rates.
expectedOutputs: Transfer learning feature extractor accuracy benchmark
Prediction confidence scores on test images
experiments.starterPrompt: Implement Transfer Learning using a pretrained MobileNetV2 model. Freeze base weights, train a custom classification head on a multi-class dataset, and report accuracy.

experiments.title: Autoencoder for Image Denoising & Dimensionality Reduction
experiments.aim: Construct an encoder-decoder Autoencoder architecture to reconstruct compressed representations and remove Gaussian noise from inputs.
experiments.description: Implement bottleneck latent representations using MSE reconstruction loss to denoise corrupt input data.
expectedOutputs: Side-by-side comparison: Original, Noisy, and Reconstructed images
experiments.starterPrompt: Build an Autoencoder for image denoising. Add Gaussian noise to input images, train the encoder-decoder network, and display side-by-side original, noisy, and denoised outputs.

experiments.title: Client-Server Socket Communication (TCP / UDP)

expectedOutputs: Server startup log: 'Server listening on port 5000...'
Client connection handshake and message transmission
Server response received and printed by client
experiments.starterPrompt: Implement a Java TCP Client-Server program. The server listens on a socket and echoes back reverse capitalized strings sent by the client. Run both processes and demonstrate successful message exchange.

experiments.title: Remote Method Invocation (Java RMI) for Distributed Computing
experiments.aim: Design and implement a distributed application using Java RMI where a remote client invokes computational methods on a remote server object.
experiments.description: Define a Remote Interface, implement the Remote Object extending UnicastRemoteObject, bind it to the rmiregistry, and look it up from the client.
expectedOutputs: Server object bound with service name in registry
Client remote method call returning calculated result
experiments.starterPrompt: Implement a distributed calculator application using Java RMI. Define the remote interface with add, subtract, and multiply methods. Implement the server, bind it to rmiregistry, and create a client that invokes each method.

experiments.title: Multi-Client Concurrent Chat Server using Multithreading
experiments.aim: Implement a multithreaded TCP server that handles multiple simultaneous client connections using worker threads or thread pools.
experiments.description: Spawn a dedicated ClientHandler thread for each incoming socket connection to broadcast messages to all active participants.
expectedOutputs: Server accepting connections from Client 1 and Client 2 simultaneously
Broadcast message from Client 1 appearing on Client 2 terminal
Graceful client disconnect handling without crashing server
experiments.starterPrompt: Build a multi-threaded Java chat server capable of handling multiple concurrent clients. Spawn two client processes and verify that messages sent by one client are received by the other.

experiments.title: Distributed Mutual Exclusion Algorithm (Token Ring / Ricart-Agrawala)
experiments.aim: Implement and simulate a distributed mutual exclusion algorithm to control access to a shared critical resource across distributed nodes.
experiments.description: Simulate a token-passing ring or timestamped request-reply protocol to guarantee safety, liveness, and freedom from starvation.
expectedOutputs: Critical Section entry and exit logs with timestamp guarantees
Mutual exclusion verification (no two nodes in critical section simultaneously)
experiments.starterPrompt: Simulate the Token Ring algorithm for distributed mutual exclusion in Java. Create 4 node processes, circulate the token, and demonstrate how a node requests and enters the critical section exclusively.

experiments.title: Leader Election in Distributed Systems (Bully Algorithm)
experiments.aim: Implement the Bully Election Algorithm to dynamically elect a new coordinator when the active leader fails in a distributed cluster.
experiments.description: Simulate node failure detection, ELECTION message broadcasting to higher-ID processes, OK responses, and COORDINATOR announcement messages.
expectedOutputs: Higher ID node winning election and broadcasting coordinator message to all alive nodes
experiments.starterPrompt: Implement the Bully election algorithm in Java. Simulate 5 processes with IDs 1 to 5. Simulate the crash of leader process 5, trigger an election from process 2, and demonstrate process 4 taking over as new coordinator.

experiments.title: Lamport's Logical Clocks for Distributed Event Ordering
experiments.aim: Implement Lamport's Logical Clock algorithm to order events across distributed processes in the absence of a synchronized physical clock.
experiments.description: Update local process clock on internal events ($C_i = C_i + 1$) and on receiving message $m$ with timestamp $t$ ($C_i = \max(C_i, t) + 1$).
expectedOutputs: Total ordering verified conforming to Lamport's 'happens-before' relation
experiments.starterPrompt: Implement Lamport's Logical Clock algorithm in Java across 3 cooperating processes. Show clock updates for internal events, message transmissions, and message receipts to enforce causal ordering.

experiments.title: Distributed MapReduce Simulation for Word Count
experiments.aim: Simulate a distributed MapReduce pipeline with Master, Mapper, and Reducer nodes for distributed text processing and aggregation.
experiments.description: Partition input text across multiple Mapper worker processes, shuffle intermediate key-value pairs, and aggregate frequencies in Reducer workers.
expectedOutputs: Mapper input partition splits and key-value emission logs
Shuffle and partition phase organizing intermediate keys
Reducer final aggregated frequency table output
experiments.starterPrompt: Create a Java distributed MapReduce simulation. Implement a Master coordinator, 2 Mapper tasks, and 1 Reducer task to perform word count on a sample distributed text corpus.

experiments.title: Distributed Shared Memory / Cache with Consistency Protocol
experiments.aim: Implement a simulated Distributed Key-Value Store or Cache with read/write replication and consistency verification across nodes.
experiments.description: Implement primary-backup replication or quorum-based reads/writes across distributed storage instances with synchronization locks.
expectedOutputs: Cluster node synchronization on write operation
Consistent read output across all replica nodes
experiments.starterPrompt: Implement a distributed in-memory key-value store in Java with a master node and replica node. Demonstrate write propagation and read consistency.
